decisions.context: Authorization needs the fraud score before it can proceed, and the brief sets a tens-of-milliseconds response target.

alternatives.label: Synchronous scoring in the authorization path
cons: Availability: scorer failure can delay authorization

alternatives.label: Asynchronous scoring after authorization
pros: Availability: authorization need not wait for scoring
cons: Latency: score arrives too late for the authorization decision

chosen.label: Synchronous scoring in the authorization path

decisions.rationale: The latency target decides this choice: authorization must receive the score in time to use it. This makes scorer availability part of the authorization path.
consequences: The authorization flow needs a defined timeout and failure behavior.

decisions.context: The service must keep working during peaks while returning scores quickly. Replicas can serve requests independently if model artifacts are available to each one.

alternatives.label: Stateless scoring replicas
pros: Peak operation: add replicas to serve more requests
Latency: score without a central inference hop
cons: Peak operation: model artifacts must be distributed to replicas

alternatives.label: Single centralized scoring service
pros: Latency: one serving endpoint to manage
cons: Peak operation: centralized capacity can become a bottleneck

decisions.rationale: Peak operation decides this choice: independent replicas can add serving capacity as load rises. It costs additional work to distribute and keep model artifacts consistent.
consequences: Deployments need to manage replica capacity and artifact consistency.

decisions.decision: Record score-time model and feature inputs
decisions.context: Auditors need to establish which model version and which features produced each score. Retaining the score-time inputs preserves that evidence if models or feature sources later change.

alternatives.label: Persist model version and feature values with each score
pros: Explainability: retain the inputs used for the score
Reproducibility: identify the scoring model version
cons: Cost: store a record for every score

alternatives.label: Persist model version and recompute features later
cons: Reproducibility: later feature sources may differ
Explainability: historical inputs may be unavailable

chosen.label: Persist model version and feature values with each score

decisions.rationale: Auditor explainability decides this choice: the actual score-time inputs and model version provide direct evidence of how the score was produced. This gives up storage cost and requires managing retained records.
consequences: Each score requires a durable record of its model version and feature values.
Retention and access controls for these records need definition.

uncovered: Timeout and fallback behavior when scoring is unavailable
